title: Kian's Dry Boat Parade
markdown:
Kian loved to measure things — how tall a flower is, or how many fluffy clouds puff up. His best friend was Puddle, a bouncy green frog who loved to ribbit-ribbit and hop. And then there was Grandma Nell, with her warm hugs and brilliant ideas.

Kian, Puddle, and Grandma Nell were planning a teeny boat parade. Little boats from leaves and twigs, floating down the sparkly stream. “This will be the most amazingest parade ever!” croaked Puddle. Then he looked at the stream. Big froggy eyes blinked. “Kian, what if water splashes? Our passengers will be all wet and drippy!”

Wet and drippy passengers. A pickle. Their first idea was a big leaf roof. WHOOSH. A little wave splashed over it. Not dry enough. Next, a fluffy dandelion puff. SPLISH. SPLASH. It got all mushy — yucky mushy. “This is tricky-tricky-tricky!” wriggled Puddle.

Water stays out. Passengers stay dry.

“We need something water just can’t get through,” hummed Kian, tapping his chin. He remembered Grandma Nell’s bright red umbrella and her shiny green boots. “Grandma Nell! Can you help us find something that keeps our passengers super dry?” Nell smiled her warmest smile. “Let’s look closely. Things that don’t let water through.”

They found a smooth waxy fabric, a fuzzy bit of wool, and a crinkly plastic wrapper. Kian got his measuring tape ready. “It’s time for an experiment!” Grandma Nell got a little watering can.

She poured water onto the fuzzy wool. Swoooooosh. The water soaked right in, like a thirsty sponge. Heavy and damp. “Brrr. Nope,” croaked Puddle. Next, water on the waxy fabric. Drip, drip, plop. The water rolled right off. “It’s like the water can’t stick!” Finally, water on the plastic wrapper. The water beaded up and rolled away. “Hooray!” cheered Puddle. “Those two keep the water out!”

Water stays out. Passengers stay dry.

They chose the shiny waxy fabric. Kian measured it perfectly. They shaped it into a snug roof for their boat. When they put the boat on the water, it floated. They placed a brave little ladybug inside. Splish. A little wave splashed the boat. Not a single drop got to the ladybug. She stayed perfectly dry.

“YESSSSS!” Kian did a happy dance. Puddle did a super-bouncy hop. “Our parade is saved! The driest, bestest parade ever!”

Kian beamed. “Some materials don’t let water through. Water slides off, or it can’t soak in.” Grandma Nell nodded. “That’s called being waterproof. It’s how the material is made, and how it acts with water.” Puddle wiggled his toes. “So that’s why your boots keep your feet dry, Grandma Nell!”

Kian giggled. “I wonder what other amazing things in the world work this way.” The sun shone. Their tiny boat parade began, passengers perfectly dry, ready for a splashingly good time — the splash on the outside, the dry on the in.

Water stays out. Passengers stay dry.
characters: Kian (a measure master), Puddle (a frog), Nell (a grandma)
author: StoryGen Community
